newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes mixed, boosted late by soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes mixed, boosted late by soybeans.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed with nearby contracts boosted by a late rally in soybeans, traders said.
"Wheat and corn were following in sympathy with beans plus (July) corn held support at $2.80," said Bill Biedermann of Allendale Inc.
Corn was under pressure most of the session on aggressive seedings of the U.S. corn crop, traders said.

USDA Monday said as of Sunday, U.S. corn was 71 percent seeded, well ahead of 52 percent a year ago and the 50 percent average pace. There also have been very few reports of emergence problems in the early-seeded crop despite cool weather in the U.S. Midwest.
Meteorologists said record cold temperatures were recorded overnight in Iowa and Nebraska and that the cold weather may linger through May.
Traders also cited talk that a well-known analytical firm had increased its estimate for U.S. corn acreage which may have weighed on the new crop December contract.
Corn futures closed 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 1/2 lower, with May up one at $2.89-1/4 a bushel. July closed 1-1/2 cents higher at $2.84-1/2.
Funds sold an estimated 20.0 million bushels of corn Tuesday with Smith Barney the key seller of 12.0 million bushels of July, traders said.
FIMAT Futures sold 15.0 million bushels of December and bought 4.5 million bushels of November soybeans, traders said.
Cargill Inc bought six million bushels of December and bought four million bushels of July, floor sources said.
Tenco Inc spread 5.5 million bushels of July/December at 15-1/2 to 15-3/4 cents, premium July and Cargill Inc spread four million July/May at five cents, premium May, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 63,000 contracts, above the 48,798 traded Monday.

In corn options, Merrill Lynch Futures bought 1,000 December $2.50 puts at 9-1/4 to 9-1/2 cents, Cargill Investor Services bought 800 July $3.20 calls at one cent and Prudential Securities bought 350 July $2.90 puts at 12-5/8 to 13 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, about the same as the 13,982 traded Monday.
